issues.description: TritonLoraConfig.is_registered is shared mutable state mutated without synchronization and before backend acknowledgment.
issues.detail: _get_lora_config returns the same TritonLoraConfig instance from model_metadata; _create_trtllm_generate_request flips is_registered=True without a lock and before the backend confirms registration. Concurrent first-use requests race; a request that loses the race or hits a failure leaves the flag lying, so later calls omit weights for a task_id the backend never cached. Needs a per-LoRA lock and a real registration signal.

issues.description: TritonLoraConfig collapses two distinct ADTs (vLLM vs TRT-LLM) into one all-Optional dataclass, violating LSP.
issues.detail: vLLM needs only `name`; TRT-LLM call sites index `task_id` and `path` without precondition checks. One shared dataclass with Optional fields hides the contract and lets the TRT-LLM path read fields the vLLM subtype never sets. Split into a sealed hierarchy or tagged union with non-Optional required fields per backend.

issues.description: lora_task_id allocation is non-deterministic and not unique across models or restarts.
issues.detail: task_id starts at 1 and increments per entry inside _parse_lora_configs, with no invariant tying task_id to LoRA identity across restarts or across different base models. TRT-LLM caches by task_id, so collisions can serve the wrong adapter. Assign deterministically per (model, name) — e.g., hash — and document the uniqueness specification.

issues.description: _parse_lora_configs return type annotation lies — declared List[tuple[str,str]] but returns List[TritonLoraConfig].
issues.detail: The signature is part of the contract and misleads type checkers and maintainers. Update to Optional[List[TritonLoraConfig]] or, better, return a typed LoraCatalog that also carries backend kind so downstream code stops re-deriving it from a stringly-typed flag.

issues.description: Bare `except Exception` returns None, silently conflating parse errors with 'no LoRAs configured'.
issues.detail: A malformed multi_lora.json or unrelated bug becomes invisible: the function prints a traceback and returns None, so callers cannot distinguish absence from failure. Either fail loud at startup or log a structured warning with a defined error contract — do not both print and swallow.

issues.description: Debug residue: stray `print(f"backend: {backend}")` and `print(traceback.format_exc())` in parser and routers.
issues.detail: Unconditional print statements bypass the configured logger, cannot be filtered, and will spam stdout in production. They also bundle unrelated debug churn into a feature patch. Replace with logger calls at appropriate levels and remove the per-iteration backend print before merge.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on two correctness blockers: TritonLoraConfig.is_registered is shared mutable state mutated without a lock and before backend acknowledgment, and lora_task_id allocation is non-deterministic and not guaranteed unique across models or restarts — both of which can serve the wrong adapter under load. The dataclass also collapses two distinct backend ADTs into one all-Optional shape, breaking the contract that TRT-LLM call sites rely on. Secondary issues: a wrong return type annotation, a bare `except Exception` that silently disables LoRA listing, and unconditional debug prints in production paths. NEEDS-WORK before merge.
